description: Chemical compatibility matrix for pool and spa products. Every pair with a safety-relevant interaction is explicitly recorded. Status: safe | avoid | never_mix | unknown.

records.description: Trichlor (acidic, ~pH 2.9) reacts violently with calcium hypochlorite (alkaline, strong oxidizer). Reaction generates heat, chlorine gas, and can cause fire or explosion.
records.handlingInstructions: Never combine in container, chlorinator, or skimmer. If accidental mixture occurs, evacuate and call emergency services.

records.description: Mixing muriatic acid with any chlorine product releases chlorine gas — a toxic, corrosive gas that causes severe respiratory damage.
records.handlingInstructions: Never combine. Add to pool water separately, at least 30 minutes apart with pump running.

records.description: Acid mixed with calcium hypochlorite releases chlorine gas and can cause fire. Extremely hazardous.
Both are acidic but combining concentrated forms releases chlorine gas.
records.handlingInstructions: Never combine. Add separately to pool.

records.description: Mixing oxidizers can produce rapid decomposition, heat, oxygen release, fire, or explosion.
records.handlingInstructions: Never combine. These products are from incompatible sanitizer systems.

records.description: Biguanide (PHMB) is completely incompatible with all chlorine products. Mixing causes precipitation and destroys both sanitizers.
records.handlingInstructions: Full water replacement required when switching between systems.

records.description: Both are chlorinated isocyanurates but mixing concentrated forms generates heat and can cause degradation or fire risk.
records.handlingInstructions: Do not add simultaneously to chlorinator or skimmer. Add separately to pool water.

records.description: Adding soda ash immediately after calcium hypochlorite can cause calcium carbonate precipitation and water cloudiness.
records.handlingInstructions: Add at least 4 hours apart. Allow each to fully disperse before adding the next.

records.description: Adding algaecide simultaneously with chlorine shock may reduce effectiveness of both. Chlorine can oxidize some algaecide types.
records.handlingInstructions: Add algaecide 24 hours after shocking, when FC has returned to normal range.

records.description: Sodium bicarbonate and sodium hypochlorite are compatible. Can be added to pool within normal maintenance intervals.
records.handlingInstructions: Add each product separately to pool with pump running. No special precautions needed.

records.description: Both are alkaline sodium compounds. Compatible when added separately to pool water.
records.handlingInstructions: Standard handling. Pre-dissolve each before adding.

records.description: Adding calcium chloride and baking soda simultaneously to pool water may cause calcium carbonate to precipitate, causing cloudiness.
records.handlingInstructions: Add at least 4–6 hours apart. Calcium chloride first, allow to fully distribute, then baking soda.

records.description: Acid and bicarbonate react rapidly, releasing CO2, heat, and causing foaming overflow. Dangerous in concentrated form.
records.handlingInstructions: Never mix directly. In pool water, each can be used at separate times as normal.

records.description: Sodium chloride and sodium hypochlorite are compatible. Used together in salt pool maintenance.
records.handlingInstructions: Standard handling. Add salt in shallow end, add chlorine near return jets.

records.description: Chlorine and acid products must never be stored together. Even vapors can react.
records.handlingInstructions: Store in separate, ventilated locations. Separate by at least 10 feet or in separate storage structures.
